approach: Add an `athena.focus/1` record (records/focus/<month>/<id>.json, fields id, at, text, set_by), loaded into `Records.focus`; the greatest id is the current focus. `Athena::set_focus` and `current_focus` back `athena focus [text]`, and `StatusView.focus` makes `athena status` print it. Add `[priority_caps]` (urgent = 3, high = 10) to the schema and athena.toml. The cap logic is pure code in plan.rs: `Plan::build_capped(entries, history, &PriorityCaps)` runs an `apply_caps` pass on the dependency-raised tiers and stores one `Demotion` per demoted item in `Plan.demoted`. `build_with` delegates with no caps. The pass obeys three rules from the revision. (1) An item whose own latest person priority record names the tier being capped is never demoted; it counts toward the cap, and non-person items go first. (2) Prerequisites of kept items are kept in the same tier (a closure), so a kept dependent never sits behind a demoted prerequisite. (3) Only person records whose level equals the capped tier count as person-set. `priority_violations` applies `Plan.demoted`. `drain.rs` `prepare` (shared by `athena plan` and `drain`) gets the caps from a new defaulted `Steps::priority_caps`, which `RealSteps` overrides from athena.toml and the priority records. `display::plan` prints one `demoted` line per demotion. Planning writes no record. A binary-level test runs the real `athena plan` end to end.

decisions.choice: Cap inside Plan::build_capped on the dependency-raised effective tiers; keep the result in Plan.demoted; leave PlanEntry.priority untouched.
decisions.reason: The request caps effective priorities. Rewriting entry.priority would be undone when a dependent raises a prerequisite, and it would change what callers print. Plan.demoted lets priority_violations and the printout use the same tiers.

rejected.why: Misses dependency raising and mutates the entries callers print.

rejected.option: Add a priority_set_at field to PlanEntry
rejected.why: About 12 PlanEntry literals in drain.rs, tests/drain.rs and plan.rs would need edits. A side map in PriorityCaps avoids that.

decisions.choice: Person-set items are never demoted (answers finding 2). In a capped tier, `protected` = items whose person-set level equals that tier. They are kept even if they alone exceed the cap. The remaining slots go to the rest, ordered (rung, age) as build_with already sorts a wave. The sort is: person-set first, newest `at` first, then the rest. When no person-set items exist, plan order decides.
decisions.reason: The accepted reading says an item with a person's priority record is never demoted below its own record. The request's 'person-set first, newest first' ordering still applies as the tiebreak among person-set items when ranking which prerequisites or fill slots come first. The cap can be exceeded only by person-set items and prerequisite closure, never by plan-ordered fill.

rejected.option: Demote the oldest-set person item when person items exceed the cap (previous Decision 3)
rejected.why: Contradicts the accepted reading, and the earlier 'wins' test (a Normal item among urgent ones) could not fail.

decisions.choice: Keep prerequisites of kept items (answers finding 3). apply_caps builds the kept set as protected ∪ ranked fill, and each kept item also keeps its transitive prerequisites that sit in the same tier. Fill stops once the kept count reaches the cap. Closure members count toward the count and can exceed the cap. The high pass reruns the same logic on the post-urgent tiers.
decisions.reason: effective_priorities raises a prerequisite to its dependent's tier; priority_violations flags any earlier item with a lower tier. Keeping the closure means a demoted dependent never lets a demoted prerequisite sit behind a kept item, and a kept dependent never has a demoted prerequisite. Dependents demoted together with their prerequisite end at the same tier or lower, so no violation arises. Also, priority_violations applies Plan.demoted to its effective tiers.

rejected.option: Treat open question 5 as harmless and ignore dependencies
rejected.why: The drain turns each priority_violations flag into a 'plan order contradicts priority' note.
Equivalent in effect but would change the printed demotion after the fact; deciding it while choosing the kept set gives one correct line per item.

decisions.choice: PriorityCaps.person_set is BTreeMap<String, (Priority, Timestamp)>: job id to the level and `at` of its highest-n priority record. apply_caps treats an item as person-set in tier T only when the level equals T (answers finding 6).
decisions.reason: An item a person set to normal that a dependency raised to urgent is not a person's urgent choice, so it can be demoted like any other.

rejected.option: Count any priority record as person-set
rejected.why: Would protect an item in a tier the person never chose.

decisions.choice: Take the caps and person-set data through a new defaulted trait method `Steps::priority_caps(&self) -> PriorityCaps` (default: no caps). RealSteps overrides it from `self.athena`'s Config and `self.records()`. drain.rs is a required extra file (finding 1).
decisions.reason: The only production caller is drain.rs `prepare` (`Plan::build_with` at about line 2008), which `athena plan` and `drain` share. Config and records reach it only through Steps. A default of no caps leaves every fake Steps impl compiling. drain.rs is outside the listed deliverables but has no substitute; the scope check should allow it, and the summary will say so.

rejected.why: plan.rs is pure; it should not read config.
Forces edits to about 10 fake impls, including tests/drain.rs.

decisions.choice: Name the section `[priority_caps]` with `urgent = 3` and `high = 10` as a #[serde(default)] struct with deny_unknown_fields. Reset it in Config::reading_inputs and extend the reading_inputs test.
decisions.reason: Matches how `[parallel]` works: old configs still parse and readings' config digest does not change.

decisions.choice: Cascade the high pass: items demoted from urgent count in the high tier, and the excess drops to normal. One Demotion per item records the final from and to, and a second demotion merges into the first.
decisions.reason: Follows the accepted reading, which says demoted items count toward the high cap.

rejected.option: Demote each item at most one tier and let high exceed 10

decisions.choice: set_by from `Git::config_get("user.name")` (athena-git); refuse if empty. Latest focus = greatest id; the id is RecordId::from_parts(at, n) with n above any existing id of the same timestamp.
decisions.reason: Priority records carry no identity, so git's user.name is the available source. Ids are time-ordered, and the counter keeps two focuses in one second ordered.

decisions.choice: No refusal_corpus case is added. The cap demotes tiers and refuses or matches no input, and Priority::from_text and the request format are unchanged.
decisions.reason: The corpus requirement applies only to rules that refuse or match input.
